description: THE COMMON CORE FOR MINNESOTA: SECURING SAFETY AND HEALTH WITH DATA TO ACTION THROUGH OUR STATE INJURY PREVENTION PROGRAM. - UNINTENTIONAL INJURIES KILLED MORE THAN 4,700 MINNESOTANS DURING 2016-2019 AND LED TO ABOUT 1.3 MILLION EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT AND HOSPITAL VISITS. MORE THAN 1,700 MINNESOTANS DIED IN TRAFFIC CRASHES DURING THE SAME 4-YEAR PERIOD, AND ALMOST 97,000 MINNESOTANS WERE TREATED FOR INJURIES DUE TO TRAFFIC CRASHES IN EMERGENCY DEPARTMENTS AND HOSPITALS. MOST UNINTENTIONAL INJURIES ARE PREDICTABLE AND PREVENTABLE. THIS APPLICATION DESCRIBES THE CURRENT CAPACITY OF THE MINNESOTA DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH AND ITS INJURY AND VIOLENCE PREVENTION SECTION (IVPS). IT DETAILS THE HISTORY OF THE PROGRAM AND NOTES ITS SUCCESS IN BUILDING PARTNERSHIPS AND DATA SYSTEMS THAT ALLOW US TO FULLY EMBRACE AND PARTICIPATE IN TRUE DATA-TO-ACTION, IN PARTICULAR WITH HARD-TO-REACH POPULATION GROUPS.  THIS APPLICATION DETAILS HOW MDH IVPS PLANS TO STRENGTHEN THREE KEY AREAS: PREVENTING ACES, IMPROVING TRANSPORTATION SAFETY, AND SUPPORTING THE RESPONSE TO TBI-RELATED INJURIES. THE WORK PROPOSED FOLLOWS AN OUTLINE THAT MDH IVPS HAS USED TO SERVE MINNESOTANS FOR MANY YEARS: COLLECT DATA THROUGH EXCELLENT SURVEILLANCE TO LEARN THE PATTERNS OF HEALTH OUTCOMES; SHARE THESE DATA WITH RELEVANT ORGANIZATIONS, AGENCIES, AND PEOPLE; WORK TOGETHER TO MAKE EVIDENCE-BASED DECISIONS ABOUT ACTIONS TO ADDRESS THE FACTORS IMPACTING THE OUTCOMES; AND EVALUATE THE ACTIONS TO LEARN LESSONS FOR FUTURE PROGRAMMING. THROUGH PARTNERSHIPS WITH KEY ORGANIZATIONS AND AGENCIES, MDH IVPS AIMS TO DECREASE DISPARITIES IN ACES, TRANSPORTATION-RELATED INJURIES, AND TBI INCIDENCE BY EXPLORING SHARED RISK AND PROTECTIVE FACTORS WHICH WILL, IN TURN, PREVENT A MULTITUDE OF OTHER INJURIES. NOTABLY, MDH IS APPLYING FOR THE ENHANCED OPPORTUNITY WITH A MULTI-METHOD, MULTI-COMPONENT EVALUATION OF THE IMPACT OF OUR NOVEL SURVEILLANCE STRATEGY USING THE MN SYNDROMIC SURVEILLANCE PIPELINE TO INFORM THE RESOURCE FACILITATION (RF) SERVICE THAT IS OFFERED TO PEOPLE LIVING WITH A TBI. FIRST, RF PARTICIPANTS? SHARED RISK AND PROTEC TIVE FACTORS (SRPFS) WILL BE EXPLORED TO IDENTIFY WHO IS USING THIS SERVICE TO INFORM IMPROVEMENT OF FUTURE RECRUITMENT STRATEGIES. SECOND, FOCUS POPULATIONS THAT EXPERIENCE TBIS AT A DISPROPORTIONATE RATE AND MAY BE PARTICULARLY DIFFICULT TO RECRUIT TO RF WITH ITS CURRENT RECRUITMENT METHODS WILL BE CONSULTED ON HOW TO BEST MEET THEIR NEEDS THROUGH RF. THIRD, PEOPLE WHO INITIALLY DID NOT PARTICIPATE IN RF UPON THE FIRST CONTACT ATTEMPT WILL BE RECONTACTED TO DETERMINE THE NEED FOR SUCH A RECONTACTING STRATEGY AND, IF FOUND TO BE NEEDED, DETERMINE THE MOST IMPACTFUL WAY TO RECONTACT PEOPLE WHO HAVE BEEN LIVING WITH A TBI FOR AN EXTENDED PERIOD OF TIME. WE ANTICIPATE A NATIONAL AUDIENCE FOR THIS WORK. THE ADDITIONAL MOTIVATING IMPETUS BEHIND THIS APPLICATION IS THE DISSATISFACTION WITH THE STATUS QUO. WHILE MINNESOTA OVERALL ENJOYS GOOD HEALTH, THERE ARE POPULATION GROUPS (DEFINED BY GEOGRAPHY OR ZIP CODE, AGE GROUP, GENDER, INCOME AND RACE) THAT HAVE DISPROPORTIONATELY HIGH RATES OF ACES, MOTOR VEHICLE CRASH AND OTHER TRANSPORTATION-RELATED INJURY, AND TRAUMATIC BRAIN INJURY.AS A RESULT OF INVESTING IN MINNESOTA THROUGH THIS FUNDING OPPORTUNITY, INJURY PREVENTION AND CONTROL EFFORTS WILL BE ROOTED IN DATA, IMPLEMENTED IN PARTNERSHIP WITH COMMUNITIES AND FELLOW GOVERNMENT AGENCIES, FOCUSED ON POPULATIONS WHO EXPERIENCE INJURY INEQUITABLY, EVALUATED TO DISCOVER PROSPECTS FOR REPLICATION AND OPPORTUNITIES FOR IMPROVEMENT, AND RAISED AT POLICY-LEVEL MEETINGS TO SUPPORT THE GREATEST IMPACT. WITHOUT THIS FUNDING IN MINNESOTA, CORE INJURY PREVENTION INFRASTRUCTURE WILL BE COMPROMISED CERTAINLY AND CURTAILED TO A GREAT DEGREE. THIS HOPE FOR PREVENTION DRIVES THIS APPLICATION.

Eligible applicants include:   U.S. state governments or their bona fide agents; U.S. territorial governments or their bona fide agents; and political subdivisions of states, which includes local governments such as counties, cities, townships, and special districts or their bona fide agents. If applying as a bona fide agent of a state, territory, or local government, a legal binding agreement from the state, territory, or local government as documentation of the status is required. Only one application will be funded from each eligible state or territory. Funded recipient must have access to state or territory-wide data sources. 

This program is authorized under sections 392(a)(1) of the Public Health Service Act, as amended (42 USC § 280b-0(a)(1)).

cfda_info.cfda_objectives:
NON-RESEARCH STATE AND COMMUNITY PROGRAM GRANTS/COOPERATIVE AGREEMENTS:  To develop, implement, and promote effective injury and violence prevention and control practices.
  
RESEARCH GRANTS: (1) To support injury control research on priority issues; (2) to integrate aspects of engineering, public health, behavioral sciences, medicine, engineering, health policy, economics and other disciplines in order to prevent and control injuries more effectively; (3) to rigorously apply and evaluate current and new interventions, methods, and strategies that focus on the prevention and control of injuries; (4) to stimulate and support Injury Control Research Centers (ICRCs) in academic institutions which will develop a comprehensive and integrated approach to injury control research and training; (5) to bring the knowledge and expertise of ICRCs to bear on the development of effective public health programs for injury control and (6) Embed health equity and a focus on the conditions of communities and spaces where we live, play, work and learn into all of the Center’s scientific and programmatic work
